arxiv-1808-03139.title: Low Ply Drawings of Trees and 2-Trees
arxiv-1808-03139.creator: Michael T. Goodrich, Timothy Johnson
arxiv-1808-03139.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Michael T. Goodrich, Timothy Johnson. Ply number is a recently developed graph drawing metric inspired by studying road networks. Informally, for each vertex v v , which is associated with a point in the plane, a disk is drawn centered on v v with a radius that is α \alpha times the length of the longest edge incident to v v , for some constant α ∈ ( 0 , 0.5 ] \alpha\in(0,0.5] .

arxiv-2208-05080.title: Mathematical measures of societal polarisation
arxiv-2208-05080.creator: Johnathan A. Adams
arxiv-2208-05080.description: Abstract \AppendGraphicsExtensions .tif Abstract In opinion dynamics, as in general usage, polarisation is subjective. To understand polarisation, we need to develop more precise methods to measure the agreement in society. This paper presents four mathematical measures of polarisation derived from graph and network representations of societies and information-theoretic divergences or distance metrics.

arxiv-2309-08285.title: One-class knowledge distillation for spoofing speech detection
arxiv-2309-08285.creator: Jingze Lu, Yuxiang Zhang, Wenchao Wang, Zengqiang Shang, Pengyuan Zhang
arxiv-2309-08285.description: Abstract The detection of spoofing speech generated by unseen algorithms remains an unresolved challenge. One reason for the lack of generalization ability is traditional detecting systems follow the binary classification paradigm, which inherently assumes the possession of prior knowledge of spoofing speech.

arxiv-2403-04785.title: Large Language Multimodal Models for 5-Year Chronic Disease Cohort Prediction Using EHR Data
arxiv-2403-04785.creator: Jun-En Ding, Phan Nguyen Minh Thao, Wen-Chih Peng, Jian-Zhe Wang, Chun-Cheng Chug, Min-Chen Hsieh, Yun-Chien Tseng, Ling Chen, Dongsheng Luo, Chenwei Wu, Chi-Te Wang, Pei-fu Chen, Feng Liu, Fang-Ming Hung
arxiv-2403-04785.description: Abstract Chronic diseases such as diabetes are the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Numerous research studies have been attempted with various deep learning models in diagnosis. However, most previous studies had certain limitations, including using publicly available datasets (e.g. MIMIC), and imbalanced data.

arxiv-2506-16917.title: Error analysis of BDF schemes for the evolutionary incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
arxiv-2506-16917.creator: Bosco García-Archilla, Volker John, Julia Novo
arxiv-2506-16917.description: Abstract Error bounds for fully discrete schemes for the evolutionary incompressible Navier–Stokes equations are derived in this paper. For the time integration we apply BDF- q q methods, q ≤ 5 q\leq 5 , for which error bounds for q ≥ 3 q\geq 3 cannot be found in the literature. Inf-sup stable mixed finite elements are used as spatial approximation.

arxiv-2512-07628.title: MoCA: Mixture-of-Components Attention for Scalable Compositional 3D Generation
arxiv-2512-07628.creator: Zhiqi Li, Wenhuan Li, Tengfei Wang, Zhenwei Wang, Junta Wu, Haoyuan Wang, Yunhan Yang, Zehuan Huang, Yang Li, Chunchao Guo, Peidong Liu
arxiv-2512-07628.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhiqi Li, Wenhuan Li, Tengfei Wang, Zhenwei Wang, Junta Wu, Haoyuan Wang, Yunhan Yang, Zehuan Huang, Yang Li, Chunchao Guo, Peidong Liu. Compositionality is critical for 3D object and scene generation, but existing part-aware 3D generation methods suffer from poor scalability due to quadratic global attention costs when increasing the number of components.

arxiv-2512-24281.title: Safe Sliding Mode Control for Marine Vessels Using High-Order Control Barrier Functions and Fast Projection
arxiv-2512-24281.creator: Spyridon Syntakas, Kostas Vlachos
arxiv-2512-24281.description: Abstract This paper presents a novel safe control framework that integrates Sliding Mode Control (SMC), High-Order Control Barrier Functions (HOCBFs) with state-dependent adaptiveness and a lightweight projection for collision-free navigation of an over-actuated 3-DOF marine surface vessel subjected to strong environmental disturbances (wind, waves, and current).

arxiv-2602-06995.creator: Konstantinos Gounis, Sotiris A. Tegos, Dimitrios Tyrovolas
arxiv-2602-06995.description: Abstract The availability of commercial wireless communication and sensing equipment combined with the advancements in intelligent autonomous systems paves the way towards robust joint communications and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Autonomous vehicles are one of the several applications that directly benefits from millimeter-wave (mmWave) access, enabling improved communications and accurate localization in the interest of control and navigation.

pmc-11397188.title: Comprehensive Serum Proteomic and Metabolomic Profiles of Pediatric Patients with Moyamoya Disease Reveal Core Pathways
pmc-11397188.creator: Qingbao Guo, Manli Xie, Qian-Nan Wang, Jingjie Li, Simeng Liu, Xiaopeng Wang, Dan Yu, Zhengxing Zou, Gan Gao, Qian Zhang, Fangbin Hao, Jie Feng, Rimiao Yang, Minjie Wang, Heguan Fu, Xiangyang Bao, Lian Duan
pmc-11397188.description: BackgroundMoyamoya disease (MMD) signifies a cerebrovascular disorder with obscure origin and a more rapid and severe progression in children than adults. This investigation aims to uncover age-associated distinctions through proteomic and metabolomic profiling to gain insights into the underlying mechanisms of MMD.

pmc-12471762.title: Analytical Approaches to the Rapid Characterisation of Marine Glycolipids in Bioproduct Discovery
pmc-12471762.creator: Sudarshan Dhakal, Tim D. Nalder, Susan N. Marshall, Colin J. Barrow
pmc-12471762.description: Glycolipids are structurally diverse amphiphilic molecules with potential as non-petrochemical-derived bioproducts, including surfactants, emulsifiers, and antioxidants. The different bioactivities associated with this range of glycolipid structures also present opportunities for dietary supplements, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. Marine glycolipids are underexplored due to challenges with purification and structural characterisation.

pmc-12558526.title: User informed design of oral dispersible strips (ODS) to deliver pediatric antiretroviral therapy in Kenya: A mixed methods evaluation of product preferences and acceptability
pmc-12558526.creator: Sarah Finocchario-Kessler, May Maloba, Catherine Wexler, Fred Were, George Mugendi, Yvonne Mbithi, Zachary Nicolay, Michael Hageman, Shadrack Babu, Nicodemus Maosa, Kara Knapp, Gregory Thomas, Sally Maliski, Edward Maliski
pmc-12558526.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundInnovation to streamline the administration of pediatric antiretroviral therapy to infants and small children is urgently needed. The objective of this study was to assess user acceptability of key characteristics of prototype placebo oral dispersible strips (ODS) that would contain a pediatric HIV regimen of abacavir + lamivudine+ dolutegravir (ALD), and the extent to which they would address current barriers to ART adherence.MethodsWe conducted 7 focus group discussions with 64 caregivers across three hospitals; 3 FGD with 25 pediatric healthcare providers; and

pmc-12595024.title: Hybrid optimized remaining useful life prediction framework for lithium-ion batteries with limited data samples
pmc-12595024.creator: Md Ibrahim, Shaheer Ansari, Afida Ayob, M. S. Hossain Lipu, Maher G. M. Abdolrasol, Abdul Waheed Khawaja, Muhammad Amir Khalil, Daniel Ioan Stroe
pmc-12595024.description: This study introduces a Jellyfish optimization technique integrated with a Multi-Layer Perceptron, specifically a Feedforward Neural Network (FNN) model, for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). A multiple battery with multi-input (MBMI) profile is utilized to create 91-dimensional data features for model training. A systematic sampling approach is employed to extract relevant data features.

pmc-12610303.title: Perforator-Sparing Microsurgical Clipping of Tandem Dominant-Hemisphere Middle Cerebral Artery Aneurysms: Geometry-Guided Reconstruction of a Wide-Neck Bifurcation and Dorsal M1 Fusiform Lesion
pmc-12610303.creator: Matei Șerban, Corneliu Toader, Răzvan-Adrian Covache-Busuioc
pmc-12610303.description: Background and Clinical Significance: Tandem pathology at the dominant-hemisphere middle cerebral artery (MCA)—combining a wide-neck bifurcation aneurysm that shares the neck with both M2 origins and a short dorsal M1 fusiform dilation embedded in the lenticulostriate belt—compresses the therapeutic margin and complicates device-first pathways.

pmc-13081188.title: Implementation of Integrated Telemedicine Services in Resource‐Limited Somalia: A Case Study of Baano Healthcare Technology
pmc-13081188.creator: Najib Isse Dirie, Mohamed Mustaf Ahmed, Ahmed Adam Mohamed
pmc-13081188.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSomalia′s healthcare system faces significant challenges due to limited infrastructure and physician density (2.5 per 10,000 population). Telemedicine is a promising solution, particularly given the country′s mobile phone penetration rate of 54%.

pmc-13107185.title: Proteomic analysis across Healthy–NAT–Tumor tissues uncovers clinically relevant biological events in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-13107185.creator: Wei Liu, Wei Wang, Dan-Wei Zheng, Ying-Qin Ran, Ming-Xiao Feng, Dan-Xia Deng, Xiu-E Xu, Li-Yan Xu, Hai-Hua Huang, En-Min Li
pmc-13107185.description: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a highly lethal malignancy with limited therapeutic progress and a 5-year survival rate below 20%. Normal adjacent-to-tumor (NAT) tissues, widely used as “normal” controls, are increasingly recognized as molecularly distinct from both tumor and healthy tissues, reflecting early carcinogenic alterations rather than a true normal state.

pmc-13365855.title: Integrated hearing and genetic screening for neonatal deafness in a resource-limited region: insights from Qingyuan, China
pmc-13365855.creator: Qin She, Hui-Lin Ou, Er-Fang Tang, Wei Huang, Wei-He Tan, Mu-Lan Zeng, Xiu-Feng Pan, Chen-Bing Liu
pmc-13365855.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveThis study aimed to delineate the prevalence and mutation spectrum of deafness-associated genes among newborns in a resource-limited region of China, and to assess the diagnostic yield of combined hearing and genetic screening.MethodsFrom May 2017 to May 2023, 22,819 newborns underwent concurrent hearing screening and genetic screening for deafness-associated mutations using 9-variant or 23-variant microarrays targeting GJB2, SLC26A4, GJB3, and mitochondrial 12SrRNA. Whole-exome sequencing was performed in selected cases with inconclusive results.

pmc-13379186.title: Reply to Comment on Ultrasonographic Measurements of the Liver, Gallbladder, and Hepatic Vessels among University-aged Youth in Baghdad, Iraq
pmc-13379186.creator: Abdul Sattar Arif Khammas
pmc-13379186.description: l concerns raised and clarify our methodology. RESPONSE TO METHODOLOGICAL CONCERNS REGARDING CENTRAL OBESITY CLASSIFICATION Prof. Al-Mendalawi addresses an important point about the classification approach which is used to define central obesity (CO) in our study. We agree that determining proper anthropometric cut-off values is crucial for accurately diagnosing CO and interpreting research outcomes.

pmc-13474016.title: Adaptive multi-stage domain unlearning for white-matter lesion segmentation
pmc-13474016.creator: Domen Preložnik, Žiga Špiclin
pmc-13474016.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionInter-scanner variability in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) adversely affects the diagnostic and prognostic quality of scans and necessitates the development of models that are robust to domain shift arising from the unseen scanner data.

pmc-13536156.title: Hamstring muscle injury rehabilitation in sports: a scoping review
pmc-13536156.creator: Aïda Cadellans-Arróniz, Caroline Prince, Spyridon Iatropoulos, Jurdan Mendiguchia, Kenny Guex, Jean-Benoît Morin, Alexandre Rambaud, Pascal Edouard
pmc-13536156.description: ObjectiveTo describe the methodological characteristics and content of published hamstring muscle injury (HMI) rehabilitation programmes in order to inform clinical practice and guide future research.MethodsWe searched the MEDLINE (PubMed), Scopus and Web of Science electronic databases, on October 2024, using key terms “hamstring” and “rehabilitation”, with strategies refined after a preliminary search.
